subject: MSA / Order Form - DPA and SCCs: transfer exceptions and clarifications
messages:
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@brightpathhealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@brightpathhealth.com>, Alan West <alan.west@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass and questions

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightPath is keen to proceed but legal has a few sticking points in the DPA and the SCCs references inside the Order Form. I attached our markups (BrightPath_DPA_redline_20280207.docx) and an annotated matrix (SCCs_Execution_Matrix_20280207.xlsx).

High level:
- We have three requested edits around controller/processor language and one carveout ask for model training data retention.
- We also asked for confirmation on any subprocessor list and whether Redwood will provide transfer impact analysis for EU-to-US pathways.
- Our procurement/legal team flagged the indemnity/limitation cross-reference in the MSA that ties to the Order Form — they want to understand exposure if we require additional export controls.

Can you confirm who on Redwood legal will lead the DPA conversation and whether you can provide a short transfer impact addendum? We’d like to get to a redline that legal can sign off by the end of next week.

Thanks — attaching the files.

Regards,
Claire Johnson
Head of Procurement, BrightPath Health
Claire Johnson

Date: Wed, 08 Feb 2028 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass and questions

Claire — thanks for the redlines and matrix. I’ve looped in Laura (legal) and Ben (account lead) and Kim in case we need hosting/region level inputs.

High-level response:
- We can accept clarifying edits around controller/processor language with one change to the model-training carveout (we need to keep a narrow telemetry retention clause for service quality). Laura, I’ll defer to you on language.
- We can provide a transfer impact addendum draft; we typically offer an EU->US transfer mechanism via SCCs + documented TIA, but we’ll need to confirm subprocessor locations and any KMS constraints.
- On the indemnity/limitation piece: I proposed below two options for BrightPath legal — 1) keep current MSA language and add limited export-control carveout in Order Form, or 2) accept revised cap language tied to Order Form addendum that explicitly references export controls. Ben — can you advise commercial trade-offs on option 2?

Next steps:
1) Laura to send proposed DPA counter-redlines (we’ll include inline change notes).
2) We will produce a transfer impact addendum draft by EOD Friday for your review.
3) Propose a 30-minute legal sync Wed/Thu next week to walk the remaining items.

Date: Thu, 09 Feb 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass and questions

Claire / Sergio — I reviewed BrightPath’s markups and added inline comments (see attached "redline_comments.pdf"). Summary of legal view and proposed counter-language:

1) Roles (Controller / Processor) — maintain current MSA role assignments but adopt BrightPath’s suggested clarification in DPA section 1.2 with the following tweak: replace "sole discretion" with "written instructions provided by controller" to reduce ambiguity.
2) SCCs — Redwood will adopt the EU standard contractual clauses for controller-to-processor transfers, and we will append a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA). The TIA will document technical/organizational measures and subprocessor geographies.
3) Subprocessors & Evidence — BrightPath asked for a current subprocessor list and onboarding SLA. We can provide the list and will include a 30-day notice for new subprocessors; for high-risk subprocessors we propose a 60-day notice.
4) Model training data carveout — we cannot agree to a broad carveout that allows retention of customer data for model training. We can agree to retain anonymized telemetry for 30 days for debugging/perf, and only with BrightPath opt-in for longer retention for explicit research purposes.
5) Indemnity/Limitations — we will not reopen the MSA commercial cap broadly. However, we can add a narrowly scoped export-control carveout in the Order Form that addresses additional liabilities triggered by BrightPath-specific export compliance obligations.

I’ve highlighted proposed phrasing inline; if BrightPath accepts the TIA template we’ll finalize the counters and share a single consolidated redline.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

Attachments: redline_comments.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@brightpathhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@brightpathhealth.com>, Alan West <alan.west@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass and questions

Laura — appreciate the careful read and the TIA commitment. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The model-training carveout as written in your note is close to acceptable; we will need explicit opt-in language in the Order Form for any research retention. Can you add the opt-in as a simple checkbox clause in the Order Form annex?
- For the TIA, will Redwood document key rotation and where keys are held (KMS region)? We need that evidence for our audit.
- Regarding subprocessors: a rolling list is fine; for any subprocessors processing EU personal data we will require a signed Data Processing Addendum or equivalent documentation.

Procurement asks if Redwood can guarantee data residency in EU for production workloads as an ordering option (we want to reduce transfer paths). If not guaranteed, we need an explicit fallback: what happens if capacity is not available in EU (can you route to dedicated EU long-term or is there a transient US fallback?).

Happy to take the consolidated redline. If you can turn that around by EOD Friday we’ll aim to have internal signoff early next week.

Best,
Claire

Claire — quick commercial note from our side:

We can offer an EU-residency ordering option for production instances as part of the Order Form (EU Dedicated) with a 30% premium on standard hosted pricing to cover regional capacity guarantees. If EU Dedicated is not available within the requested SLA window, our fallback is to route to closest regional capacity with explicit notice and a temporary data escrow (we log ingress/egress and provide a contractual commitment to data deletion after termination).

If BrightPath prefers not to take the EU Dedicated upgrade, we can still proceed with our standard hosted option plus the TIA and additional assurances around KMS key region and subprocessors. The commercial trade-off is cost vs guaranteed locality.

Next steps from commercial:
- I’ll attach a short Order Form addendum draft (pricing + locality checkbox) and a DocuSign envelope for the pilot clause.
- If that looks ok we can move the updated Order Form into the legal queue.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass and questions

Claire — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clarity. Summary and agreed next steps so we have a single point of truth: 

1) Redwood legal will produce a consolidated DPA redline (Laura) and a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) that documents SCC usage, subprocessor geographies, and KMS region/key rotation practices. Expect these by EOD Friday (2028-02-17).
2) Commercial proposal: Ben has provided an EU Dedicated ordering option (pricing in addendum). BrightPath can choose EU Dedicated to guarantee residency; otherwise the standard hosted option will include the TIA and the transient fallback with logs/escrow and deletion commitments.
3) Model-training retention: Redwood will include an explicit opt-in checkbox in the Order Form annex; default behavior is 30-day anonymized telemetry only.
4) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide current list and 30-day notice for additions (60 days for high-risk).
5) DocuSign: Ben will share the Order Form addendum envelope; we’ll push redlines into a single doc for your legal review.

Proposed legal sync: Wednesday 2028-02-22 at 09:00 PT (30 minutes) — please confirm and Ben will send the invite.

If that matches your expectations we’ll produce the consolidated set and share links to the draft documents.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this pilot.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
(415) 555-0187
